thread:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Dedicated pool velora-med-vpc GPU exhaustion detected. 100% GPUs in use, queue depth rising -> potential customer impact for tenant velora-med. Severity: P1. https://redwood.internal/incidents/3487650123
priya_s: paging @sre_oncall — Velora reporting errors and timeouts. Can you take the pager? :rotating_light:
sre_oncall: ack, taking pager. I'm pulling pool metrics and recent deploys.
miguel_r: looking at task histograms: massive spike in batch job from velora-analytics around 17:22 UTC, long-running beam jobs pinning GPUs.
alice_prod: customer ticket INC-4589 showing 500s on their prod inference endpoints. Support on call with them now.
sre_oncall: quick check: autoscale policy for velora-med-vpc is set to static (no cross-tenant burst) due to data isolation. Need decision: allow emergency burst into shared-spare or provision ephemeral dedicated nodes. @priya_s @miguel_r
priya_s: product/security needs to sign off on any cross-tenant burst. @kyle_support can you confirm customer policy on cross-tenant compute? :eyes:
kyle_support: on the call with Velora PM now. They explicitly forbid cross-tenant compute for PHI compliance. No burst into shared if it touches other tenant data. They authorized temporary degraded-quality fallback but not mixed-tenant compute.
miguel_r: understood. Option B: spin up additional capacity in the same VPC (ephemeral dedicated nodes) — infra can allocate A100s but ~10-15m currently. Can we also swap to a smaller model to reduce GPU utilization while infra finishes provisioning?
sre_oncall: starting provisioning flow. Running: ```
# allocate ephemeral nodes in velora-med-vpc
rdev infra allocate --tenant velora-med --gpus 4 --type a100-80 --ephemeral --priority emergency
```incident-bot: Provisioning job queued (task id: prov-3487650123). ETA estimate 14m.
alice_prod: product suggests a quantized fallback model for immediate relief. Risk: potential quality regression. Need explicit customer consent.
kyle_support: Velora gave verbal okay for temporary degraded quality for up to 30 minutes while they fix their job. Documented in the call notes.
priya_s: product approves fallback for 30m with telemetry. Plan: (1) route a fraction of traffic to quantized model v1.2-q, (2) provision 4x A100s, (3) rehydrate full traffic when nodes ready. Agreed?
sre_oncall: implementing route change now. Command: ```
redwood route update --tenant velora-med --model rwlq/velora-v1.2-quant --traffic 100 --max-tokens 512
``` Applying low-level config: reducing max sequence length and enforcing smaller batch sizes to keep latency predictable.
miguel_r: provisioning update: nodes booting, attaching to velora-med-pool. Health checks pending.
incident-bot: Provisioning started -> prov-3487650123 status: started.
sre_oncall: monitoring queues... queue depth decreasing after model fallback. Latency 95th dropping from 2.8s -> 0.9s.
miguel_r: infra reports nodes attached and registered. Finalizing rebalancer.
incident-bot: prov-3487650123 status: succeeded. 4x a100-80 added to velora-med-vpc.
sre_oncall: scaling traffic back to primary model gradually. Observability shows stable CPU/GPU headroom now. Queues drained. Marking immediate mitigations as: model-fallback + ephemeral nodes provisioned.
priya_s: notes for follow-up/postmortem: 1) add an emergency-burst contract option for enterprise tenants with strict guardrails, 2) reduce ephemeral provisioning SLA from 15m -> 5m, 3) add automated detection to suggest fallback models earlier. Assign to eng-postmortem.
eng-postmortem: assigned. We'll run a blameless postmortem and include timeline + root cause (customer batch job oversight + lack of fast-provision path).
incident-bot: INC-3487650123 created and updated: status P1 -> P2 after mitigation. Handing off to postmortem.
sre_oncall: handing off pager. I'm off-call. :white_check_mark:
priya_s: thanks everyone. I'll coordinate customer comms and follow-up actions.
